config.title: usePrevious

intro.title: usePrevious
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom hook called usePrevious in Angular to track and display the previous value of a state variable. You will learn the core concept of using a ref to persist a value across component re-renders without triggering updates. The main technologies involved are Angular's framework with TypeScript, using signals for state management and the effect function for side effects. By the end, you will understand how to capture a value before it changes and apply this pattern in your own projects.
intro.usecase: The usePrevious pattern is essential in Angular applications where you need to track value changes over time. In dashboard components, it helps detect when a metric's value crosses a threshold to trigger visual alerts or notifications. Form validation benefits from comparing current and previous field values to show meaningful change-based error messages. Interactive data tables use it to preserve previous filter states, enabling undo functionality or showing what data changed after filtering.

objectives: Implement a custom hook that tracks and returns the previous value of a state variable
Apply the usePrevious hook to monitor changes in component state or props
Initialize and update the previous value reference within the hook's effect
Integrate the usePrevious hook into functional components to access prior values
Render component output that displays both current and previous values
Manipulate the hook's return value to conditionally trigger side effects
Configure the hook to handle different data types including primitives and objects

steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add two properties: currentValue of type number initialized to 0, and previousValue of type number | undefined initialized to undefined.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript property syntax with type annotations and initial values in the class body.

steps.hint: Use this.currentValue = 0; inside the ngOnInit method body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method will initialize currentValue to 0 when the component loads.
successCriteria: currentValue is set to 0 inside the ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're setting this.currentValue = 0 inside the ngOnInit method.

steps.title: Create updateValue method to change currentValue
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, create a method named updateValue that takes a number parameter and sets currentValue to that number.
steps.hint: Define a method with the signature updateValue(newValue: number) and assign newValue to this.currentValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have an updateValue method that can change the currentValue property.
successCriteria: The updateValue method is defined with a number parameter and assigns it to this.currentValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your updateValue method takes a number parameter and assigns it to this.currentValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateValue method isn't defined correctly. It should be a method inside the AppComponent class that updates currentValue with a new number value.

steps.title: Implement usePrevious logic in updateValue
steps.instruction: Inside the updateValue method, store the current value of currentValue into previousValue before updating currentValue to a new random number.
steps.hint: Assign this.previousValue = this.currentValue before changing this.currentValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The updateValue method now implements the core usePrevious pattern by preserving the previous value before updating the current value.
successCriteria: The updateValue method correctly assigns this.previousValue = this.currentValue before updating this.currentValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're saving the current value to previousValue BEFORE changing currentValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the order of operations. You need to save currentValue to previousValue first, then update currentValue.
